title: Session Paging Garbage Collector — proto notes
content:
Context and intent:
- Personal sketch: reconcile long-lived session memory with limited KV cache footprint on GPU nodes. Trying to design a lightweight "session paging + GC" proto that can run in the serving runtime and cooperate with client-side prefetch heuristics.
- Goal: avoid OOMs for noisy tenants, keep hot prefixes on-GPU, cold material on SSD, and allow fast resume of recently active sessions with minimal RPCs.

Design constraints / non-goals:
- Must be compatible with existing KV cache (prefix + full token keying) and streaming generation.
- Prefer eventual consistency between routing layer and node-local pager (no global lock).
- Non-goal: full transactional session persistence (we do lightweight snapshots only).

High level idea:
1) Each session is a sequence of "pages" (logical contiguous ranges of context tokens); pages are the unit of resident memory.
2) Node-local pager keeps an LRU-ish metadata table for pages (resident, in-ssd, remote).
3) When memory pressure crosses threshold, pager selects victim pages using a cost heuristic (size, last_access_ms, instruction_hotness, tenant_qos).
4) Victim pages are asynchronously serialized to the local node SSD in a compact delta format and marked non-resident.
5) On access to non-resident page, runtime issues a resume request: preferably local SSD read; fallback to fetch-from-backend (remote store) if not on node.
6) Lightweight GC pass reclaims pages that are stale beyond TTL or belong to closed sessions; GC can be opportunistic (during low load).

Data structures (sketch):
- PageMeta { page_id: string, session_id: string, start_token_idx: int, length_tokens: int, resident_bytes: int, on_ssd: bool, last_access_ms: int, touch_count: int, tenant_id: string, hot_score: float }
- NodePagerState: map(page_id -> PageMeta) + resident_bytes_total + resident_limit_bytes + async_write_queue

Victim selection heuristic (proto):
score = alpha * recency_score + beta * (1 / size_mb) + gamma * tenant_penalty - delta * api_hotness
- recency_score = exp(-(now - last_access_ms)/decay_ms)
- tenant_penalty = large number if tenant over-QPS or QoS lower tier (to protect SLOs for premium tenants)
- api_hotness = hints from tracing/prefix-probability (if generation repeatedly reuses the page)

On-disk format (compact delta):
- page header: session_id | page_id | start_idx | token_count | base_hash
- payload: compressed token bytes + small kv of token->embedding pointer offsets (optional)
- target: small enough to load subset of page without decompressing whole session if possible

API shapes (sketch)
- POST /internal/v1/pager/evict
  body: { "node_id": "node-13", "victims": [ { "page_id": "p:abc", "session_id": "s:123", "reason": "oom-pressure", "priority": "background" } ] }
  response: { "accepted": true, "async_write_ids": ["w-42"] }

- POST /internal/v1/pager/resume
  body: { "node_id": "node-13", "page_id": "p:abc", "session_hint": { "preferred_source": "ssd|remote" } }
  response: { "state": "resumed|queued|missing", "location": "ssd|remote", "estimated_ms": 12 }

- GET /internal/v1/pager/meta?session_id=s:123 -> returns list(PageMeta) (paginated)

Config sketch (runtime flags; YAML for readability):
pager:
  resident_limit_bytes: 40GB
  eviction_threshold_percent: 0.85    # start async eviction when resident > threshold*limit
  aggressive_threshold_percent: 0.95  # synchronously block new allocs and prioritise eviction
  ssd_write_parallelism: 4
  ssd_path: "/var/lib/redwood/pager"
  page_ttl_ms: 604800000   # 7 days for inactive pages (configurable per-tenant)
  decay_ms: 600000         # recency decay for scoring (10m)
  tenant_penalty_map:      # per-tenant controls, can be set from control plane
    default: 1.0
    premium: 0.2
    noisy-tenant-group: 3.0

Interaction patterns with client prefetch heuristics (notes):
- Client can submit 'prefetch hints' during session activity: {prefetch_pages: [p1,p2], priority: immediate|soft, expected_ttfb_ms}
- Runtime will try to keep prefetched pages resident; hints add to hot_score for heuristic.
- Hints are best-effort and do not guarantee residency (tenant penalties can override).

GC and lifecycle rules:
- Soft GC (opportunistic): reclaim pages with hot_score < threshold and last_access > page_ttl_ms. Runs in background low-cpu windows.
- Hard GC (reactive): when resident > aggressive_threshold, synchronously evict until below eviction_threshold. Hard GC respects pinned pages (client pinned for immediate resume) and premium tenant protection.
- Final GC for closed sessions: when session closed signal seen (session state machine), enqueue full session snapshot to cold store for long-term retention, then mark all pages deletable after retention TTL.

Telemetry / metrics to emit (proto):
- pager.resident_bytes_total
- pager.evictions.count (labels: reason, tenant_id, node_id)
- pager.evict_write_ms.p95
- pager.resume.latency.p50/p95 (ssd|remote)
- pager.page_hit_ratio (resident hits / total page requests)
- pager.prefetch_hint_effectiveness (hints accepted / hints requested)
- pager.gc_cycles.count

Resilience and failure modes:
- SSD write fails: mark page on_ssd=false, escalate to remote-copy async task; if both fail, mark page missing and notify control plane for backfill.
- Node crash while page non-resident: metadata persists to local WAL; on restart, pager reconciles WAL with local disk and control-plane index.
- Race conditions: multiple nodes may try to fetch the same page from remote simultaneously; introduce a per-node fetch backoff and a short-lived distributed lease (control-plane) to avoid storm.

Open questions / tradeoffs:
- How big should page granularity be? Tokens-per-page vs bytes-per-page. Small pages = better partial-resume, higher metadata overhead. Large pages = fewer IOs but larger latency when missing. Suggest 128–1024 token range for initial experiments.
- Should the control plane hold a global page index (which node has which page on SSD)? Pros: faster remote routing. Cons: control-plane churn and consistency headaches. Maybe optional for dedicated clusters.
- How to surface correctness for clients that rely on exact session determinism? If we resume from compressed deltas there is risk of tiny de-synchronization. Need snapshot/verification hash in header (base_hash) and fallback re-fetch entire session on mismatch.
- Cost model for eviction decisions: include estimated re-fetch cost (read_ms + network_ms) vs memory bytes freed. Can derive from historical telemetry.

Short worked example (ASCII diagram):
[client] --(stream)-> [ingress router] --(route)-> [node-A: serving runtime]
node-A memory: [page p1 resident][p2 resident][p3 non-resident->ssd][p4 resident]
                                |
                                | disk: /var/lib/redwood/pager/p3.delta.gz
                                |
on-pressure: p1/p2 active, p3 cold
pressures: allocation triggers -> choose victim: p2 score low -> POST /internal/v1/pager/evict -> async write w-42 -> mark non-resident
client later requests token at idx inside p2 -> runtime checks NodePagerState -> not resident -> POST /internal/v1/pager/resume -> SSD read -> populate memory -> continue generation

Implementation plan (next steps):
- Spike: implement PageMeta + local pager runloop in a branch. Minimal: SSD write/read + resident accounting. (2 weeks)
- Instrument: add telemetry events for evict/resume/hit-ratio. (1 week)
- Experiment: run on canary pool with synthetic workload (noisy tenants) to tune thresholds. (2–3 weeks)
- Decide: integrate with control-plane global index or keep node-local only for first ship.

Notes to self / TODOs:
- [ ] confirm compression codec: zstd16 for write/read tradeoff
- [ ] prototype small-page layout to allow partial decompress of section (preferable)
- [ ] add safety checksum in header (sha256) and mismatch recovery path
- [ ] add tenant-aware eviction policy knobs to control plane UI
- [ ] write e2e test sim that spawns 500 concurrent sessions with skewed access pattern

References / related tickets:
- GH PR 7890: background writer overhaul (linked above)
- INFRA-4123: observed OOM on node-13 in week of 2025-01-10 (noisy tenant pattern)

Rough timeline for iteration: 6–8 weeks to hardened alpha on canary cluster (node-local only), 3–4 more weeks to integrate global index if decided.

Unresolved: how we signal client pinned pages safely across rollouts (pin format, TTL, and revocation) — followup with SDK/Client folks (Maya).

End of scratchpad. This is intentionally fuzzy in spots; want to get a minimal prototype into the runtime to gather real telemetry and iterate.
